paper.title: Enhancing strength and ductility in Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C austenitic low-density steels through Ni and Cr alloying synergy adding
paper.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
paper.paper_scope: Develops four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr austenitic low-density steels (3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr) by hot rolling plus online ultrafast cooling, and investigates how Ni and Cr alloying controls the precipitation of nanoscale κ-carbides/LRO domains and thereby the strength–ductility balance, strengthening mechanisms and deformation behaviour.

processes.process_name: Hot rolling with online ultrafast cooling (HR + UFC)
processes.description: Ingots vacuum induction melted under high-purity Ar, homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h, then hot-rolled (initial 1040–1060 °C, finishing 950–970 °C) to 4 mm-thick sheet with 95% thickness reduction, and finally online ultrafast cooled (UFC) to ambient temperature at ~40 °C/s using the in-house ADCOS-PM device.
processes.processes_notes: The identical thermo-mechanical processing route was applied to all four Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr alloys; because the process/终态 is shared across all alloys it is defined once with alloy_id left null, and the four samples differ only by composition.

unmapped_findings: Microstructure of all four UFCed steels is a single equiaxed FCC γ-austenite phase with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries; no B2/BCC phase found. Average grain sizes (excluding twins) are 7.63, 8.95, 8.57 and 7.60 μm and (including twins) 3.51, 3.73, 3.72 and 2.2 μm for 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr respectively.

Nanoscale ordered structures differ by composition: 3Cr and 2Ni5Cr (higher Cr) form ellipsoidal LRO domains (~1.75 nm and ~2.14 nm), whereas 2Ni and 2Ni3Cr (higher Ni) form cuboidal orthorhombic κ-carbides (2Ni has the largest, ~10 nm).

First-principles (DFT/Materials Project) formation energies of possible κ-carbide structures: (Fe,Mn)3AlC = -0.160 eV/atom, Cr21(FeC3)2 = -0.049 eV/atom, Fe2NiC = +0.082 eV/atom, AlNi3C = -0.181 eV/atom. Cr raises and Ni lowers the κ-carbide nucleation energy barrier.
Tensile properties reported (Table 2): 3Cr YS 969 / TS 1141 MPa / TEL 54.4%; 2Ni YS 1202 / TS 1283 MPa / TEL 34.1%; 2Ni3Cr YS 1110 / TS 1206 MPa / TEL 45.9%; 2Ni5Cr YS 1071 / TS 1187 MPa / TEL 50.5%.

Yield-strength modelling decomposes σys into friction, solid-solution, grain-boundary and precipitation (ordering + coherency + modulus) contributions; solution strengthening is the dominant mechanism. The results were benchmarked against literature Fe-Al, Fe-Mn, Fe-Mn-C, Fe-Mn-Al-C and stainless steels.

Deformation substructure evolution was studied by interrupted tensile tests at engineering strains of 3% (or 5%) and 10%, and to fracture (LD); 3Cr is dominated by HDDA and dynamic slip-band refinement, while 2Ni is dominated by planar slip with κ-carbide shearing, with no deformation twins detected in 2Ni.
